title: Pointwise relative cocones over simplicial parameters
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and small simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the join cone $K^{\triangleright}$ and relative colimit diagrams as in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories in a fixed containing universe. Let $B,K$ be small simplicial sets and suppose given maps $a:B\times K\to\mathcal C$ and $h:B\times K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$ such that $Ua=h|_{B\times K}$. For each vertex $b\in B$, suppose a $U$-colimit diagram $c_b:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ has been specified with $c_b|_K=a|_{\{b\}\times K}$ and $Uc_b=h|_{\{b\}\times K^{\triangleright}}$. There exists $c:B\times K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ restricting exactly to $a$ and to every $c_b$, and satisfying $Uc=h$. Moreover, for any map $c:B\times K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction at every vertex $b$ is a $U$-colimit diagram, its transpose $K^{\triangleright}\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)$ is a $U_B$-colimit diagram, where $U_B:\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal D)$ is postcomposition. Neither $B$ nor $K$ is required to be a quasicategory or weakly contractible. No cocartesian structure on $U$ and no other colimit existence are assumed.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.8.8 (02XG), equation relative-colimit-pointwise-existence, for existence with all specified vertex cocones fixed; Proposition 7.1.8.10 (02XK), with its simplicial subset A empty, for relative universality after transposition. Read online; these are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Use the quasicategory and degreewise-pullback conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Put $L=K^{\triangleright}$, $F=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$, $G=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, $H=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$, $J=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$ and $T=G\times_J H$. All four functor simplicial sets are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The pure-factor inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$ is degreewise injective by the join formula in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. The restriction clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to the quasicategory $\mathcal D$, makes $v:H\to J$ an isofibration, hence an inner fibration. This does not apply the isofibration assertion to $U$. The pullback $T$ is a quasicategory: given an inner horn in $T$, extend its $G$-coordinate to a simplex since $G$ is a quasicategory, map that simplex to $J$, and use the inner-fibration property of $v$ to extend the $H$-coordinate over exactly that $J$-simplex. The two coordinates give the required inner-horn filler in the degreewise pullback.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.7, restriction-corner construction; Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3) for restriction. Pullback horn argument written out here.

proof.text:
Use internal functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the lifting convention of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Define $r:F\to T$ by $r(u)=(u|_K,Uu)$. This is an inner fibration. Indeed, transposing an inner-horn lifting problem for $r$ gives a lifting problem for $U$ whose left map, up to interchanging factors, is
$$(L\times\Lambda_i^n)\amalg_{K\times\Lambda_i^n}(K\times\Delta^n)\longrightarrow L\times\Delta^n.$$
The inner horn inclusion is inner anodyne because every inner fibration lifts it, and $K\hookrightarrow L$ is degreewise injective. Thus [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] makes the displayed map inner anodyne. Its defining lifting property against the inner fibration $U$ supplies a filler with both restriction and base fixed. Transposition gives the required filler for $r$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.7, induced inner fibration, using Proposition 4.1.4.1; explicit pushout-product lifting argument.

proof.text:
We now compare mapping spaces of $T$ with a path pullback, without assuming $U$ an isofibration. For vertices $x,y\in T$, let $x_Z,y_Z$ be their coordinates in $Z=G,H,J$, and use the arrow mapping spaces $U_Z(x_Z,y_Z)$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. A simplex in $U_T(x,y)$ is a map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to T$ with constant endpoints. Giving such a map is exactly giving its $G$- and $H$-coordinate maps with constant endpoints and equal composites to $J$. Consequently there is a degreewise identity, commuting with every operator,
$$U_T(x,y)=U_G(x_G,y_G)\times_{U_J(x_J,y_J)}U_H(x_H,y_H).$$
All these arrow mapping spaces are Kan. Since $v:H\to J$ is an inner fibration by step 1, the final assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] says that $U_H(x_H,y_H)\to U_J(x_J,y_J)$ is a Kan fibration. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to obtain a weak homotopy equivalence
$$c_U:U_T(x,y)\longrightarrow P(U_G\to U_J\leftarrow U_H)$$
by inserting the constant path. The Kan-fibration hypothesis is on restriction $v$, not on postcomposition by $U$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329); arrow mapping-space fibration Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8). Degreewise pullback calculation is agent-written.

proof.text:
Write $M_Z=\operatorname{Map}_Z(x_Z,y_Z)$ for $Z=G,H,J$ and $M_T=\operatorname{Map}_T(x,y)$, using right-pinched mapping spaces. Restriction and insertion of a constant path define $c_M:M_T\to P(M_G\to M_J\leftarrow M_H)$. The natural pinch inclusions $j_Z:M_Z\to U_Z$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] form a strictly commuting square
$$P(j_G,j_J,j_H)c_M=c_Uj_T.$$
To check this equality on an $n$-simplex, both sides first precompose the same map $\Delta^{n+1}\to T$ by the pinch map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^{n+1}$, then take its two coordinate maps and the constant interval at their common image in $J$. The pinch inclusions are homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes, hence weak homotopy equivalences. By [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], $P(j_G,j_J,j_H)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. So are $c_U$ by step 3 and $j_T$ by pinch comparison. It follows that $c_M$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: on components and each based homotopy group, cancel the isomorphism induced by $P(j_G,j_J,j_H)$ in the displayed equality. This uses exactly the weak-homotopy-equivalence convention in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5), natural pinch inclusions; Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B). Explicit comparison square and cancellation written by the agent.

proof.text:
Use weak homotopy equivalences with the component and homotopy-group meaning of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $u,t\in F$, take $x=r(u)$ and $y=r(t)$ in step 4. The constant-path comparison in the definition of a $U$-colimit diagram is the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}_F(u,t)\xrightarrow{r_*}\operatorname{Map}_T(r(u),r(t))\xrightarrow{c_M}P\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_G(u|_K,t|_K)\to\operatorname{Map}_J(Uu|_K,Ut|_K)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}_H(Uu,Ut)\bigr).$$
Indeed, on each simplex both maps record its restriction to $K$, its image under $U$, and the constant path at their equal further images. Since $c_M$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by step 4, this composite is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $r_*$ is, by cancellation on components and based homotopy groups. Quantifying over all $t\in F$, [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] and the mapping-space predicate in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] give: $u$ is a $U$-colimit diagram if and only if $u$ is $r$-initial. This is proved here for every inner fibration between quasicategories and every small $K$; no isofibration property of $U$ was used. In particular all specified $c_b$ are $r$-initial.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, condition (2), colimit dual. The inner-fibration corner comparison is proved in steps 1-5 rather than taken from the isofibration-only corner node.

proof.text: Let $P=\operatorname{sk}_0(B)$, the simplicial subset consisting of the degeneracies of vertices of $B$. It is the disjoint union of one $\Delta^0$ for each vertex. By the internal-functor definition [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the prescribed $c_b$ give a map $g:P\to F$. Transpose $a$ and $h$ to maps $B\to G$ and $B\to H$. The equation $Ua=h|_{B\times K}$ says their composites to $J$ agree, so they define $q:B\to T$. The two specified equations for each $c_b$ give $rg=q|_P$ strictly. Thus the extension problem is the lifting square $P\xrightarrow{g}F$, $B\xrightarrow{q}T$ through $r$, with $P\hookrightarrow B$ as its left map.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.7, transposed lifting square; Corollary 7.1.8.8 (02XG), choice A = sk_0(B).

proof.text: Use the degreewise products, pullbacks and internal-functor convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $P\hookrightarrow B$. Its relative skeleta begin at $P$ and have union $B$. There are no 0-cell attachments, because $P$ contains all vertices. Suppose a lift to $F$ has been defined on one skeleton over the fixed map $q$. Each attached nondegenerate $d$-simplex $\sigma$ has $d>0$, its boundary is already lifted, and its initial vertex $\sigma(0)$ lies in $P$. The boundary lift therefore takes that vertex to the prescribed $c_{\sigma(0)}$, which is $r$-initial by step 5. The boundary criterion [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] for the inner fibration $r:F\to T$ supplies a lift of $q\sigma$ agreeing on the entire boundary. Choose these fillers for the coproduct of cells, glue by its pushout, and continue over the skeleta; their compatible degreewise union is a map $\widehat c:B\to F$ with $r\widehat c=q$ and $\widehat c|_P=g$. Uncurrying gives $c:B\times L\to\mathcal C$. Its $G$-coordinate equation is $c|_{B\times K}=a$, its $H$-coordinate equation is $Uc=h$, and its restriction to $P$ fixes every $c_b$ exactly. This proves the existence clause. All fillers in this step are in $F$ over $T$, not in $\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.7, minimal-simplex extension; implemented by relative skeleta from 0077 instead of maximality; Corollary 7.1.8.8 (02XG).

proof.text: Use the inner-fibration lifting convention of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and relative initiality as in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. For the second clause let $c$ be any map with every vertex restriction a $U$-colimit, and let $\widehat c:B\to F$ be its transpose. By step 5, $\widehat c(b)$ is $r$-initial for every $b$. The functor simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(B,F)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,T)$ are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Both $r_B=\operatorname{Fun}(B,r)$ and $U_B=\operatorname{Fun}(B,U)$ are inner fibrations: transpose an inner horn against either map and apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] with the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow B$, so that its pushout-product is $B\times\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow B\times\Delta^n$. The defining inner-anodyne lifting property supplies the filler. It remains to show that the vertex $\widehat c$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,F)$ is $r_B$-initial.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.10, reduction to relative initiality; the needed inner-fibration assertions are proved directly.

proof.text: Use standard simplices and internal functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix $n>0$ and a boundary lifting problem for $r_B$ whose boundary map takes vertex $0$ to $\widehat c$. Uncurrying gives a map $f:S=\partial\Delta^n\times B\to F$ and a prescribed map $q_n:\Delta^n\times B\to T$ with $rf=q_n|_S$ and $f(0,b)=\widehat c(b)$. Filter $S\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times B$ by [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]. Every vertex belongs to $S$, since $n>0$, so no 0-cell is attached. If an attached simplex is $(\alpha,\beta):\Delta^d\to\Delta^n\times B$, then $\alpha:[d]\to[n]$ is surjective: a nonsurjective monotone map misses a vertex and lies in the corresponding proper face, which would put the simplex in $S$. Thus $\alpha(0)=0$ and $d\geq n>0$. At its initial vertex the current boundary map has the fixed value $\widehat c(\beta(0))$, which is $r$-initial by step 8. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $r:F\to T$ and the base simplex $q_n(\alpha,\beta)$ to fill this cell in $F$ over $T$. Fill the coproduct of cells, glue by each pushout, and take the compatible union. This produces $\Delta^n\times B\to F$ over $q_n$, extending all of $f$. After currying it is the required boundary filler for $r_B$. Since this works for every $n>0$ and $r_B$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, the same criterion proves $\widehat c$ is $r_B$-initial.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.10, boundary problem (7.10), A empty. Explicit product-simplex and skeletal argument, with all fillers over T.

proof.text: Use the internal-functor and right-pinched mapping-space formulas of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and relative initiality as in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. Let $\widetilde c:L\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)$ be the other transpose of $c$, and let $s$ be the restriction corner for $U_B$ along $K\hookrightarrow L$. Currying identifies $s$ with $r_B=\operatorname{Fun}(B,r)$, not with $r$. More explicitly, an $n$-simplex in its source is a map $L\times B\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$; interchange $L$ and $B$ to obtain an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,F)$. An $n$-simplex of its target is a pair of maps $K\times B\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ and $L\times B\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ whose further maps on $K\times B\times\Delta^n$ agree. Interchanging coordinates identifies this pair with an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,T)$. These bijections commute with every simplicial operator, restriction, and postcomposition, hence identify the maps $s$ and $r_B$ and the vertices $\widetilde c$ and $\widehat c$. A simplicial isomorphism induces an isomorphism on the right-pinched mapping spaces by their defining formulas, so step 9 gives $s$-initiality of $\widetilde c$. Apply the argument of steps 1-5 to the inner fibration $U_B$ (proved inner in step 8) between its functor quasicategories. Its corner is $s$, so it identifies this $s$-initiality with the $U_B$-colimit condition of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. This proves the universality clause without any additional existence hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.8.10, A empty; currying and the inner-fibration corner comparison proved in steps 1-5.

lean.statement: theorem relative_cocone_parameters {C D B K : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory C] [Quasicategory D] (U : C ⟶ D) [InnerFibration U] : (∀ (a : B ⊗ K ⟶ C) (h : B ⊗ rightJoinCone K ⟶ D), a ≫ U = (𝟙 B ⊗ₘ rightJoinConeInclusion K) ≫ h → ∀ cb : B _⦋0⦌ → (rightJoinCone K ⟶ C), (∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, IsRelativeColimitDiagram U (cb b) ∧ rightJoinConeInclusion K ≫ cb b = MonoidalClosed.curry a ≫ evaluation B C b ∧ cb b ≫ U = MonoidalClosed.curry h ≫ evaluation B D b) → ∃ c : B ⊗ rightJoinCone K ⟶ C, (𝟙 B ⊗ₘ rightJoinConeInclusion K) ≫ c = a ∧ (∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, MonoidalClosed.curry c ≫ evaluation B C b = cb b) ∧ c ≫ U = h) ∧ (∀ c : B ⊗ rightJoinCone K ⟶ C, (∀ b : B _⦋0⦌, IsRelativeColimitDiagram U (MonoidalClosed.curry c ≫ evaluation B C b)) → IsRelativeColimitDiagram ((ihom B).map U) (MonoidalClosed.curry c))
